_comment: One deliberate defect per entry, applied by scripts/mutation/run.py and then reverted.
codec           which codec's tests this is evidence about
description     what the defect is, in one line
spec            the document and clause the correct value comes from; a mutation
without one is an opinion, not a defect
symmetric       true when the defect is applied identically to the encoder and the
decoder, which is the case a round-trip test cannot see by construction
edits           exact-text replacements; count must match, so a refactor that moves
the anchor makes the harness fail loudly instead of silently testing
existing_tests  the tests that claimed to cover this code before this exercise
added_tests     the spec-anchored tests added because the existing ones did not fail
expect          the measured outcome per phase; run.py exits non-zero on a mismatch

mutations.description: wavelet A_OFFSET halved (32768 -> 16384) in wenc16 and wdec16 together
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfWav.cpp: #define A_OFFSET (1 << (NBITS - 1)) with NBITS 16, so 32768. The modulo-arithmetic round trip is exact for any offset, so only a decoder that agrees with the reference's offset reads reference files.

mutations.description: wdec14 drops the +1 in (ds + 1) >> 1, i.e. rounds the reconstructed pair the other way
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfWav.cpp wdec14: as = ms + ((ds + 1) >> 1); bs = ms - (ds >> 1).

mutations.description: the 14-bit/16-bit wavelet mode threshold moved from 1<<14 to 1<<13
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfWav.cpp wav2Encode: bool w14 = mx < (1 << 14). The threshold is not signalled in the stream; it is recomputed from the transmitted maximum, so both sides move together.

mutations.description: the short zero-run base code moved from 59 to 58 in the code-length table packer and unpacker
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfHuf.cpp: SHORT_ZEROCODE_RUN = 59, LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN = 63, SHORTEST_LONG_RUN = 2 + LONG - SHORT. The packed code-length table is part of the PIZ chunk, so the constant is wire-visible.

mutations.description: canonical codes assigned to symbols in descending instead of ascending symbol order, in all three places that build them
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfHuf.cpp hufCanonicalCodeTable: codes are handed out in increasing symbol index, so within one code length the shorter symbol index gets the smaller code. Reversing it still yields a valid prefix code that this library can decode, and misreads every reference file.

edits.old:
for symbol := minIdx; symbol <= maxIdx; symbol++ {
		length := codeLengths[symbol]
edits.new:
for symbol := maxIdx; symbol >= minIdx; symbol-- {
		length := codeLengths[symbol]

mutations.description: the B44 difference bias moved from 0x20 to 0x21 in packB44 and unpack14 together
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfB44Compressor.cpp pack(): const int bias = 0x20, and unpack14()'s bias = 0x20 << shift. The biased 6-bit differences are the packed bytes themselves.

mutations.description: unpack14 reconstructs s[8] from s[0] instead of s[4], breaking the running-difference chain
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfB44Compressor.cpp unpack14(): s[8] = s[4] + ((b[3] << 2 | b[4] >> 6) & 0x3f) << shift - bias.

mutations.description: normalised float32 -> half rounding changed from round-half-to-even to round-half-up
mutations.spec: IEEE 754-2019 clause 4.3.1 roundTiesToEven, the default rounding attribute; OpenEXR's half uses it, and the conversion is what every EXR HALF sample goes through.
mutations.note: TestRoundToNearestEven appears in both phases because it was strengthened in place rather than replaced: before this exercise its table held only 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0, none of which is a tie, and it survived this mutation. The pristine measurement is in this repository's mutation report; the expectation here is the post-strengthening one.

mutations.description: subnormal float32 -> half rounding changed from round-half-to-even to round-half-up
mutations.spec: IEEE 754-2019 clause 4.3.1: roundTiesToEven applies to subnormal results too, so 2^-25 converts to +0 and 3*2^-25 to 2^-23.

mutations.description: half exponent bias changed from 15 to 16 on both the to-half and from-half paths
mutations.spec: IEEE 754-2019 clause 3.6: binary16 has a 5-bit exponent with bias 15.

mutations.description: the DCT constants built from the reference's truncated 3.14159 literal rebuilt from full-precision pi
mutations.spec: OpenEXR internal_dwa_simd.h dctInverse8x8_scalar: a = .5f * cosf(3.14159f/4.f) and friends. The literal is part of the format: files decoded with true pi differ from the reference's own readback.

mutations.description: one entry of the JPEG luminance quantisation table changed from 10 to 11
mutations.spec: ISO/IEC 10918-1 Annex K Table K.1, reproduced in OpenEXR ImfDwaCompressor.cpp LossyDctEncoder_base_construct. Entry (0,2) is 10.

mutations.description: two entries of the zig-zag remap table swapped
mutations.spec: ISO/IEC 10918-1 Figure A.6 zig-zag scan order, as reproduced in OpenEXR's quantizeCoeffAndZigXDR remap table.

mutations.description: the chunk magic changed from 0x4854 to 0x4855 on both the write and read side
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfHTJ2KCompressor: every HTJ2K chunk starts with the two bytes 'H','T'.

mutations.description: the channel map read as EXR-channel -> J2K-component instead of J2K-component -> EXR-channel, on both the encode and the decode side
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfHTJ2KCompressor: the chunk's channel map gives, for each JPEG 2000 component in order, the index of the EXR channel it carries. The RGB triplet is placed in components 0,1,2 so the reversible colour transform of ISO/IEC 15444-1 Annex G applies to it.

mutations.description: the pooled zlib writer built at BestSpeed instead of DefaultCompression
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfZipCompressor.cpp calls compress2 with Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION; ZIPCompress documents 'default level'. RFC 1950 records the level category in FLEVEL.

mutations.description: the even/odd split point changed from (n+1)/2 to n/2 in both Interleave and Deinterleave
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfZipCompressor.cpp compress(): the first half holds ceil(n/2) even-indexed bytes, so an odd-length block puts the extra byte in the first half.

mutations.description: HTJ2KExtractPackets drops the last packet of the codestream
mutations.spec: ISO/IEC 15444-1 B.9: a codestream contains exactly one packet per (tile, layer, resolution, component, precinct). SIZ (A.5.1) gives the tile grid and component count, COD (A.6.1) gives the layer count, the decomposition levels and the precinct partition, so the packet count is fixed by the codestream's own markers and an extractor that returns fewer is losing data.

mutations.description: HTJ2KExtractPackets returns the packets in reverse codestream order
mutations.spec: ISO/IEC 15444-1 B.12 and Table A.16: packets appear in the progression order COD declares. COD SGcod here is 0 (LRCP), so the packets run layer-major, then resolution, then component, then precinct; an extractor that permutes them misaddresses every packet it returns.

mutations.description: HTJ2KExtractCodestream hands over the codestream two bytes late, past the SOC marker
mutations.spec: OpenEXR ImfHTJ2KCompressor: the chunk is a header (magic, PLEN, channel map) followed by the JPEG 2000 codestream, which by ISO/IEC 15444-1 A.4.1 begins with the SOC marker FF4F. The codestream handed to the packet parser must start exactly at the first byte after the chunk header.

mutations.description: tile offset table indexed by write order instead of tile coordinate
mutations.spec: OpenEXR file layout: a tiled part's chunk offset table is indexed by tile coordinate (level major, y level major for a ripmap, then tile row, then column). A reader looks a tile up by coordinate, so a table built in write order is only correct for the canonical order.

edits.old: if idx, err = tileChunkIndex(w.headers[part], tileX, tileY, levelX, levelY); err != nil {
edits.new: if idx, err = w.chunkIndex[part], error(nil); err != nil {

mutations.description: Header.Validate stops rejecting subsampled channels on a tiled header
mutations.spec: The format forbids subsampled channels in a tiled image; the reference refuses to open one with 'x subsampling factor is not 1 for a tiled image'.

mutations.description: multi-part version field sets the tiled flag alongside the multi-part flag
mutations.spec: The tiled and multi-part version flags are mutually exclusive: a multi-part file states each part's storage in that part's own type attribute. OpenEXR rejects the combination with EXR_ERR_FILE_BAD_HEADER.

edits.old: writer.versionField = MakeVersionField(2, false, false, false, true)
edits.new: writer.versionField = MakeVersionField(2, true, false, false, true)

mutations.description: multi-part scanline part addresses the frame buffer in image coordinates instead of relative to the data window
mutations.spec: Everywhere else in this package the frame buffer's (0,0) is the pixel at the data window's origin. A part whose data window does not start at y=0 is otherwise shifted by the origin. Unlike the others here, the pre-existing TestMultiPartOutputFile does catch this one, so it is recorded as killed in both phases: the defect shipped despite having signal in the suite, not for want of it.

mutations.description: deep scanline chunk header shortened to 20 bytes, dropping unpackedSizeOfSampleData, in writer and header size together — the shipped defect exactly
mutations.spec: A deep scanline chunk header is int y + three uint64: packed offset-table size, packed sample-data size, unpacked sample-data size. Nothing else in the chunk says how many samples it holds.
